Our research confirms that the interpretation of force majeure and related contractual clauses hinges on foreseeability, substantial performance, and allocation of risk. Key precedents include Hadley v. Baxendale (consequential damages must be foreseeable) and Jacob & Youngs v. Kent (substantial performance applies to minor breaches). Statutory frameworks such as Fed. R. Civ. P. 12(b)(6) and 56 govern motion practice. Contractual risks identified include an overbroad indemnification clause (8.1) and an unenforceable non-compete (12.1). We recommend mutual indemnification, narrowing the non-compete, and preserving claims for consequential damages in high-risk areas like data breach.
